questions.q: Why does TaskUtils extend AbstractAjaxProcessor instead of staying a plain Class.create() object?
options: So one class can support both plain server-side calls and a client-callable GlideAjax entry point at the same time
AbstractAjaxProcessor is required for every Script Include, even ones never called from the client
It makes GlideRecord queries run faster
It is required before a class can define the type property
questions.explain: Extending AbstractAjaxProcessor only matters because one method, ajaxIsUserInGroup, needs to be reachable from a Client Script via GlideAjax.

options: It throws an error
false, because groupGr.next() returns false when no matching group record is found
true, because the query ran without errors
undefined, because the method has no matching case
questions.explain: groupGr.next() returns false when the query matched zero rows, and the method explicitly returns false in that case rather than continuing.

questions.q: Why does ajaxIsUserInGroup end with `.toString()` on the result of isUserInGroup(...)?
options: Because GlideAjax always returns its answer to the browser as text, never as a native Boolean
Because toString() makes the query run faster
Because isUserInGroup returns a GlideRecord object that needs converting
It is unnecessary and only there for style
questions.explain: A GlideAjax answer always arrives client-side as a string, so the wrapper converts the Boolean true/false into the text "true"/"false" before returning.

questions.q: In formatDueDate, what does the check `glideDateTime.getNumericValue() === 0` catch that a simple `!glideDateTime` check would miss?
options: A GlideDateTime object that was constructed but never given a real date value
A GlideDateTime object that is in the future
A GlideRecord that has no due date field at all
A string value instead of an object
questions.explain: An empty GlideDateTime object still exists (so !glideDateTime is false) but holds no real date, which getNumericValue() === 0 detects.

questions.q: Why does getReferenceDisplayValue call gr.isValidField(fieldName) before calling gr.getDisplayValue(fieldName)?
options: To confirm the field actually exists on that table before trying to read it, logging a diagnostic message if it doesn't
isValidField is required before any GlideRecord query can run
getDisplayValue cannot be called on reference fields without it
It converts the field name to lowercase
questions.explain: isValidField guards against typos or table mismatches in fieldName, letting the method log a useful message and return an empty string instead of erroring.
